reviews.reasoning: Re-derived MT 72:1-5 from the staged OSHB extract. Confirmed תֵּ֑ן is the imperative governing the opening petition at v.1, and that web:Ps.72.0 = oshb:Ps.72.1 is the correct owner-mandated title pairing for this identity-numbered psalm (WEB 20 verses = MT 20 verses, no separately counted title verse). Confirmed יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט at v.4 keeps the king as 3ms subject and יִֽירָא֥וּךָ at v.5 shifts to a 3mp subject, matching the claimed seam. Noted (not a defect) that v.3's יִשְׂא֤וּ is also 3mp, but its subject is the personified mountains, not the peoples/addressee shift the row is arguing, so it does not undercut the v.5 boundary. One evidence-array defect found: boundary_evidence_refs lists oshb:Ps.72.11, a verse never named or discussed anywhere in this row's rationale (which covers only vv.1, 4 and 5), rejected_alternative (title/petition framing), or device_notes (li-Shlomo label, Book II close) — an untethered citation, most likely bled over from the adjacent row's own v.11 boundary.

Re-derived MT 72:12-15. Confirmed כִּֽי יַ֭צִּיל opens the motive clause at v.12 and that the needy/poor/no-helper petition runs through v.14's ransom language, with the jussive-form וִיחִ֗י opening v.15 as the next, formally distinct clause — the claimed seam holds on tier-1 grounds. The device_notes texture aside, however, mislabels its own count's unit: it states "42-72: YHWH 32 verses / Elohim 165 book-wide," but the underlying divine-name device data are per-psalm TOKEN/occurrence tallies of the name-forms, not counts of verses containing the name (summing the per-psalm token tallies for Psalms 42-72 reproduces exactly 32 and 165, matching the recorded Book II totals) — documented in the source inventory itself as token counts, not a verse census. A verse-count sweep of the same span would differ wherever a single verse carries more than one occurrence: Ps.72.18 alone contains both a YHWH token and an Elohim token in the same verse. This is a corroborating texture aside rather than the row's driving warrant (the row itself calls it "texture only, no boundary weight"), but the count-object label as written is factually wrong.

Ps.72.18 alone (יְהוָ֣ה ... אֱ֭לֹהִים) carries one yhwh token and one elohim token inside a single verse, demonstrating the token tally and a verse tally are not interchangeable units for this span.

reviews.reasoning: Re-derived MT 72:15-18. Confirmed וִיחִ֗י opens v.15 as a jussive ("and may he live"/"let him live"), launching the blessing chain. Both WEB quotes — the continuation at v.15 (“Men will pray for him continually. They will bless him all day long.” web:Ps.72.15) and the ellipsis-joined quote spanning v.17 (“His name endures forever ... All nations will call him blessed.” web:Ps.72.17) — byte-verify in order against the folded WEB text, confirmed by tool re-check. The "all nations" phrase genuinely recurs at v.11 and v.17 (2 occurrences), a real inclusio correctly disclosed as an observation rather than promoted to a driver. The doxology opening at v.18 (“Praise be to Yahweh God” web:Ps.72.18) is confirmed by the book's own doxology/colophon record as a formally distinct closing unit, supporting the strophe's close at v.17 rather than v.18. No span, warrant, factual, or evidence defect found.

Re-derived MT 72:18-20. Confirmed בָּר֤וּךְ opens v.18 and וּבָר֤וּךְ repeats the formula at v.19, the doubled אָ֘מֵ֥ן וְאָמֵֽן closes v.19, and the colophon כָּלּ֥וּ תְפִלּ֑וֹת opens v.20 — the row's own device count (2 baruch, 2 amen for vv.18-19) matches the boundary-doxology record exactly (baruch true at both 72.18 and 72.19; amen 0 at 72.18, amen 2 at 72.19). The book-level doxology/colophon record itself treats 72.18-20 as a single combined coda span (doxology plus colophon), so keeping the colophon in the same row as the doxology, against the rejected split, matches the book's own convention rather than contradicting it. unit_type "coda" is the term the book's own strategy assigns to exactly these four book-boundary seams, so there is no controlled-vocabulary concern. The high confidence rating is well-supported here given the doubled formula and the independent colophon marker converging on the same span. No span, warrant, factual, or evidence defect found.
